title: Regional tapered launch and A/B sentinel notes (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a lightweight operational pattern we want to experiment with for region-first launches and A/B experiments where capacity and user signal lag differ across geographies. The idea: a tapered regional activation combined with a small set of instrumented "sentinel" cohorts that reveal early quality/cost regressions before broad exposure.

High-level concept (one-liner):
- Tapered launch: gradually increase exposure per-region on a half-life schedule (traffic doubles every N hours until target).
- Sentinels: small, persistent cohorts (1–3% of region traffic) routed to an instrumented fork of the model+routing stack containing extra telemetry and tighter fallbacks. Sentinels act as the early-warning system for each deployment wave.

Why this (why different):
- Regional heterogeneity: latency, user intent, and content distribution vary by region; a global canary can miss region-specific failure modes.
- Cost-aware cadence: avoid heavy early exposure in expensive regions while still surfacing quality drift.
- Faster rollback decisions: sentinel metrics are tuned for sensitivity (high recall) so we catch regressions with minimal user impact.

Scope / when to use:
- New model variants, quantized builds, or routing changes with potential regional performance regressions.
- Multi-model experiments (A/B of model families) where traffic shaping needs to respect cost and capacity quotas per region.
- Not recommended for purely UI experiments or business-metric-only A/Bs.

Principles:
- Minimal blast radius: start small, maintain an escape hatch per-region.
- Observability-first: sentinels must expose granular prompt-level and token-level signals (latency hist, token-cost, model-confidence proxies).
- Simplicity of automation: automation should be able to pause/scale back based on a single aggregated stability score.
- Human-in-the-loop for ambiguous alerts: automatic halt for clear breaches, manual review for borderline cases.

Cohort definitions:
- Sentinel cohort (S): 0.5%–3% of region traffic. Instrumented with additional logging, golden prompt probes, and strict timeout policies.
- Pilot cohort (P): next 5% of region traffic after sentinels. Production routing but with daily manual check-ins.
- Warm cohort (W): intermediate ramp group (10%–25%) to validate scale.
- Open cohort (O): remaining traffic.

Taper schedule (example):
- Day 0: S at 0.5%
- +6 hours: evaluate signals; if green, S -> 2% and open P at 3%
- Every 12 hours: double exposure for P/W until reach target or hit a guardrail
- Full open only after 72 hours of green signals across sentinels and pilot cohort

Telemetry & sentinel signals (stability score inputs):
- Latency p95 and 99 (region-specific baselines)
- Token-cost per request (avg/95th)
- Regression probes: a small set (50–200) of golden prompts with expected ranges (tokens, quality rubric)
- Safety flags: content-moderation hit rate, hallucination proxy (e.g., contradiction detector)
- Business signals: conversion delta (if available quickly), feature-specific error rates
- User experience signals: retry rate, abandonment (client-side)

Scoring model (sketch):
- Each signal normalized to region baseline; weighted sum -> StabilityScore in [0..100].
- Example weights: latency_p99 25, token_cost95 15, probe_quality 30, safety 20, retry_rate 10.
- Thresholds: <60 -> immediate rollback; 60–75 -> pause ramp + human review; >75 -> continue ramp

Automated actions mapped to score ranges:
- Score < 60: automatic traffic reweight to fallback model by region + page the rollout-steward and oncall
- Score 60–75: pause further ramp, start 2-hour observation window, trigger async quality audits
- Score > 75: continue as scheduled, post an automated progress note in #rollout-ops

Fallback ladder (per-region):
1) Soft fallback: swap to cheaper/older variant for non-critical routes (automatic)
2) Hard fallback: route sentinel + pilot cohorts to stable model globally (manual if ambiguous)
3) Quarantine: shrink to sentinels-only while creating hotfix patch

Capacity & quota guardrails:
- Reserve 10% warm capacity for rapid rollbacks in each region to avoid cascading throttles.
- Cost cap per-region per-day that, when breached, triggers a throttle on non-sentinel traffic.

Pre-launch checklist (operational):
- Confirm sentinel instrumentation shows raw prompt/response payloads and golden-probe results (Samir)
- Create rolling chartboards for each region with StabilityScore and raw signals (Riley)
- Coordinate time windows with infra (warm-up periods for GPUs)
- Post-runbook and oncall rota for rollout-steward & SRE
- Add experiment to experiment ledger (OPT-4821) and tag related PRs

Simulation plan (small lab before real user exposure):
- Use rollout-sim repo to replay a 24h snippet of region traffic (synthetic distributions) -> run hack: PR 46 combines noise injections and latency spikes.
- Inject a 5% hallucination pattern and ensure sentinel probe precision catches it within 6 hours
- Validate automatic reweight logic in sandbox with fake PagerDuty endpoint

Measurement windows & cadence:
- Real-time: 1m fresh metrics for latency, token-cost, safety flags
- Short-term: 6h evaluation window (post-change) for initial decision
- Medium-term: 72h stabilization window before full open
- Postmortem: 7-day retrospective with regression corpora attached

Human roles & responsibilities:
- Rollout steward (product): owns hypothesis, communication, and final go/no-go
- Observability lead (SRE/observability): ensures dashboards, alerts, and probes are green
- Experiment owner (ML/product): triage quality heuristics and golden-probe failures
- Oncall (SRE): executes automated rollback or manual fallback if escalation occurs

Comms templates (quick):
- Automated progress note: "[REGION] +4h: StabilityScore 82; ramp to next stage scheduled at T+8h unless breached."
- Incident: "[REGION] ABORT: StabilityScore 52; swapped to fallback variant; paging @oncall; retrospective scheduled."

Open questions / unknowns:
- Golden probe design: how to craft probes that are representative across languages and locales without biasing model tuning?
- How to tune weights of the StabilityScore for different product surfaces (conversation vs. completion vs. rerank)?
- What is the minimal sentinel size in low-traffic regions to maintain statistical power?

Next steps / action items:
- (Samir) Draft golden-probe list for APAC and LATAM by 2024-11-12
- (Riley) Wire up a per-region StabilityScore chartboard prototype in Grafana sandbox by 2024-11-18
- (Elena) Open experiment ledger entry and tag rollout-sim PRs (OPT-4821) by 2024-11-10
- (Priya) Coordinate infra warm capacity reservation with platform-engineering (internal ticket: INF-2072)

Notes to self / operational reminders (informal):
- Lean towards higher sentinel sensitivity (more false positives) early in adoption; we can tune down noise after a few runs.
- Watch for cohort starvation: if sentinels get insufficient traffic, create synthetic probe cadence to preserve signal.
- Document any bespoke regional configs (timeouts, quantization profiles) in the experiment ledger.

Appendix (short templates):
- Experiment ledger fields we use: hypothesis, region list, sentinel_size, ramp_schedule, fallback_ladder, StabilityScore_weights, golden_probes, linked_PRs, owners
- Quick rollback command (internal): curl -X POST https://internal-api/rollouts/{region}/reweight -d '{"target":"fallback","pct":100,"reason":"stability_score<60"}'

If this looks reasonable we'll try a single-region taper in EU-west first (low cost, high traffic) and iterate based on simulation outcomes.

- rollout-sim PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-sim/pull/46
